$comment:
Provenance: read from courier at a8f15ccef11bd6148c71fbe38327d9fbebbfe2e2, and THE PUBLISHER IS NOT THERE. lib/courier/events.ex at that commit has `delivered/1`, `bounced/1`, `complained/1` and `suppressed/1`, and no `queued/1` — fleet.yml records the same fact in prose. So this schema is transcribed from courier's four sibling builders and from what `Courier.Deliver`'s payload actually contains, and it is NOT read from code that emits it.

RE-READ 2026-10-02, at courier's master HEAD `ae8a660` (a8f15cc is a reachable ancestor of it; courier has moved on and fleet.yml's sourceCommit has NOT been moved, because core-26 read two files and not the whole registry): `lib/courier/events.ex` still defines exactly `delivered/1`, `bounced/1`, `complained/1` and `suppressed/1`, and still has no `queued/1`. Three further facts, because "no builder" and "misnamed builder" are different answers and only reading the state machine tells them apart:

  1. **courier says the same thing, in courier's own words.** `lib/courier/events.ex`'s moduledoc, at that HEAD: "`courier.email.queued` has no builder because courier has no queue. The send path is synchronous and documented as such — the provider is dialled inside the request — and that type exists to make a *backlog* visible. With no backlog there is no moment at which courier could honestly emit it." `AGENTS.md` and `cafaye.yml` repeat it, and `AGENTS.md` records that `Courier.Workers` and `oban` exist and lost on one stated requirement: a 202 would answer before the suppression check has run.
  2. **There is no queued state to have been misnamed.** courier's one state machine is `Courier.Suppressions`, and its states are `nil | :undeliverable | :suppressed` (lib/courier/suppressions.ex, the fold at lines 38-41 and `state/1` at 236-247). No `:queued`. The one bounded queue courier owns is the error relay's (lib/courier/error_relay/sender.ex), which carries error reports to GlitchTip and has nothing to do with mail.
  3. **Acceptance and `courier.email.delivered` are the same moment.** `Courier.Deliver` mints `message_id = "courier-" <> Ecto.UUID.generate()` and calls the provider inside the open transaction, and `record/4` writes the `courier.email.delivered` row in that same transaction (lib/courier/deliver.ex:196 at that HEAD). There is no earlier event to publish, which is why the backlog this type would report is structurally zero rather than merely unmeasured.

So the type is **declared-and-unimplemented** — core's own phrase, and the one `fleet.yml` already uses for it — rather than misnamed, and it stays in the tree: see D38. What has to be revisited the day courier builds `queued/1` is this comment, the `description` beside it, and the obligation neither can discharge alone: a builder is a shape, not an emission (courier's phrase), so a builder appearing is the moment somebody checks whether anyone calls it.
title: courier.email.queued payload
description: The `data` payload of the `courier.email.queued` event — a message accepted for delivery, emitted on acceptance rather than on send so a queue backlog is visible before it becomes a support ticket. **NOBODY EMITS THIS. The type is declared-and-unimplemented**, which is `fleet.yml`'s phrase for it and a different statement from "a consumer may subscribe and wait forever" happening by accident: courier lists `courier.email.queued` in `exposes.events` and in `Courier.Events.types/0`, and there is no `queued/1` builder in `lib/courier/events.ex` and no caller for one, at either the commit `fleet.yml` records or courier's `master` HEAD `ae8a660` (re-read 2026-10-02; the evidence and the three facts that rule out a misnaming are in this file's `$comment`). Courier's send path is synchronous by design — the provider is dialled inside the request — so there is no backlog to report and no moment at which the event could honestly be published; courier's own module doc says so in those words. **A consumer subscribing to this type waits forever, and that is a decision rather than an oversight.** The four fields below are transcribed from courier's sibling builders and from what `Courier.Deliver`'s payload contains, so they describe the shape a `queued/1` would have; they are not a record of an emission. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md and D38.

message_id.description: The notification. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`, and equal to the `message_id` on the `courier.email.delivered`, `.bounced` and `.complained` events about the same send — which is what lets a consumer measure how long a message waited.

user_id.description: The user the message is for. A bare uuid, not a cafaye-prefixed id: that is what identity emits. The two used not to join, because this repository said otherwise about identity's own events — see D7, whose second half was false, and D35 for the correction.

notification_type.description: Which of courier's messages this was. courier registers its types at boot (config or COURIER_NOTIFIERS_DIR), so the set is not frozen here.

email.description: The address the message goes to, as the caller supplied it. Present because a consumer that has to ask "who is this for?" in order to act on it will not — and because a suppression decision is about an address.
